rationale: Round-2 re-derivation at 8193ca97 (bead worktree, left byte-identical; go build clean). MY TWO CORE ASKS ARE DELIVERED AND VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: I ran all six new e2e tests live — TestNextSelection_EmitOnlyDefaultPick_PrintsLineAndSelectsRow1 (16.2s), TestNextSelection_ClaimDefaultPick_PrintsLineAndClaimsRow1 (77.2s), TestNextSelection_PositionalEmitOnly_BypassesSpecFilter (11.7s), both NegativePick tests, and the hostile-ID render test — ALL PASS against real bd. Text verification: the tests pin wantLine = 'Defaulting to item 1 (bd ready priority order). Use --pick=N or a bead ID to select a specific item.' — byte-identical to the plan's OQ-5 pinned wording — and wantBypassLine = 'emit-only: bead fetched by ID; readiness not checked.' — the implemented text, containing the spec's R6.3(a) quoted string as its prefix. Both are now genuinely red-on-revert (a Contains assertion on the exact text). The default-line tests additionally prove the RULE, not just the line: the claim-path test asserts displayed row 1 (the higher-priority bead) ends up in_progress while row 2 stays open; the emit-only test asserts the primer's '**Bead**:' line names row 1. The bypass test matches R6.3(a)'s specified shape exactly (title-unreferenced ready bead, preview proceeds, exact bypass line, no 'excluded' report, no readiness-shaped claim). I also reviewed the G2/G3 code changes riding this commit: G2's early pick<0 check at the shared RunE entry is correct (runEmitOnly is only reachable through it, message text matches SelectWork's own retained check, --pick=0 sentinel preserved and now help-documented) and its zero-side-effects tests are real; G3's termsafe.Escape-vs-idrender.Bead discrimination (free-form selector vs required-full-ID position) is the right convention split and each new render leg carries a hostile-ESC pin plus a clean-short-form byte-identical pin. No OQ-5 or pinned-wording regression anywhere in the delta. ONE RESIDUAL BLOCKS: my round-1 F2 was delivered without its explicit rider — the partial-exclusion NOTICE print is still revert-silent (F6). It is narrow and cheap, but it was a stated concrete_changes_required clause and it guards an AC-10 sub-clause ('a partial filter exclusion prints the excluded count and reason'), on a message string this bead introduced — the same revert-silence class this panel just fixed for the other two lines.
concrete_changes_required: F6 (residual of round-1 F2's rider, AC-10 partial-exclusion clause): add one CLI-level assertion that the partial-exclusion notice is actually PRINTED on a set-constructing path. Today `grep -rn 'excluded by spec filter' --include='*_test.go' cmd/` returns zero hits and ExclusionNotice is only content-pinned at unit level (readyset_test.go:202), so deleting BOTH `fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, notice)` sites in cmd/mindspec/next.go (claim path and runEmitOnly) leaves the whole suite green while silently voiding AC-10's 'a partial filter exclusion prints the excluded count and reason alongside the displayed list'. Smallest fix: one new e2e test on the nextSelectionTwoReadyBeads shape plus ONE extra title-unreferenced bead under the same epic — run `mindspec next --spec <s> --emit-only` (or the claim path), assert output contains '1 ready bead(s) excluded by spec filter' (and still selects/claims displayed row 1 of the FILTERED list). One path suffices; both print sites share ReadySet.ExclusionNotice so a single wiring pin per path-family is proportionate — but at least one must exist.
